factorRatings.note: The Infatuation rated it 7.4/10, saying the New York-style pizza has grown inconsistent since its early days — standard red-sauced pies now read as 'underseasoned' — but singled out the pastrami pie (everything-bagel-spiced crust, gruyere fondue, caramelized onion, pickles) as the one order that 'has stood the test of time beautifully.' It's a casual pizza-and-bar room in South Park from chef Sam Crannell, formerly of LloydMartin, with a creative menu that also runs to a breakfast pie and a wild boar ragu pie with fried sage and Funyuns.

Seattle magazine praised the 'sturdy, chewy-crusted' wood-fired pies at this Admiral District spot from owner Cary Kemp, who trained at Sorbillo in Naples; the review calls out buffalo mozzarella added midway through the bake to protect the crust, house-sliced prosciutto, and a wood-oven clam special served with blistered, Parmesan-dusted flatbread. It is West Seattle's only VPN-certified Neapolitan kitchen, running an imported wood oven and Italian '00' flour and San Marzano-style tomatoes.
